title: Validate progress against measurable outcomes
baseline_ref: brief/f-15 (#796, open). The card lists no merge dependency, but it validates F-15's goal measurements, so F-15's measurement model is the real stack prerequisite, as F-19 is for Q-16. Main c06b16c1 has no goal measurements.

status.capability_ready: a goal counted from cited entries, one per counted thing, with duplicate detection, correction lineage, replay receipts and routes behind F-15's goalMeasurements capability; active only where F-15 is enabled

design.checkpoint: UI-35; no visual changes in Q-17 (the dashboard presentation of entries is D-track work)

ownership.independent_reviewer: pending; Lapo coordinates technical review and shared-file integration

merge_after: F-15 (#796): this branch is stacked on brief/f-15
enable_after: F-15: the same goalMeasurements capability (JARVIS_BRIEF_GOAL_MEASUREMENTS=1); no flag of its own
decisions: One cited entry per counted thing (owner decision, 14 October): each signed partner is its own entry naming who, when it happened and the source version it came from, recorded or confirmed by the person. Provider-verified records only were not chosen.

The number is derived from the entries (owner decision, 14 October): a counted goal's value is the number of distinct things whose latest entry counts them; nobody types it. A typed total with supporting entries was not chosen.
Parent goals stay independent (owner decision, 14 October), as F-15 has them: a child's entries never change its parent. An opt-in union of a subtree was not chosen.
Counts of distinct things first (owner decision, 14 October): signed partners, customers, deals, hires. Amounts such as revenue stay on F-15's typed snapshot.
behavior: A goal can be defined as a counted measure (unit, whole-number baseline, larger whole-number target up to 1,000). Its value is the number of distinct things whose latest cited entry counts them, its score the existing absolute progress, never a delta. Defining it replaces a typed total, so the value becomes the count of cited entries; defining it again keeps the entries; the unit stays once entries count.

An entry names the thing (compared without case, width or spacing differences), when it happened (not in the future) and a cited source version, and is `counted` or `retracted`. A thing counts once per goal; a source version is cited once per goal and may support other goals; a correction names the thing's latest entry and each entry is corrected at most once, so every thing keeps one lineage. A retraction lowers the count; a later count raises it again; a detail correction keeps the count and writes no progress entry.

Entries, the count, the snapshot, the score, progress history and the goal_measurement_recorded event (basis observations, entryId, kind, corrects) commit in one immediate transaction. Exact replay returns the receipt, including after a restart; reusing a request ID with different content conflicts.

On a counted goal a typed total, a legacy score and a work result's goalScore are refused; automatic reviews still cannot score it (a passed work result cited by a review is rejected with no_verified_score_mapping). Activity notes and accepted or checked work never create an entry.

The Brief read keeps the kinds apart: a counted measure has measurementDefinition.basis observations and one observation reference per counted thing; a typed total has basis reported and one source reference. Qualification stays user_reported: entries are the person's citations, not provider verification.

Routes under F-15's capability, authentication, no-store and 8 KiB rules: POST /api/brief/goals/:id/measurement/counted, POST and GET /api/brief/goals/:id/observations (GET ?requestId= recovers a receipt).

manual_checks: Not run against a live daemon: the fixtures need no provider, model or dashboard, and the dashboard presentation of entries is D-track work. The quick path below names a manual check over HTTP.

quick_verify.manual: On a dev daemon with JARVIS_BRIEF_GOAL_MEASUREMENTS=1: POST /api/brief/goals/<id>/measurement/counted {"requestId":"c1","revision":0,"definition":{"unit":"signed partners","baseline":0,"target":10}}, then POST /api/brief/goals/<id>/observations six times with distinct subjects and source versions; GET /api/brief/goals/<id> shows value 6, score 0.6 and six observation references; posting the same partner again answers 409.
quick_verify.screenshot: not applicable: no visible UI changes

migration: Additive: table goal_observation, and optional snapshot fields basis and counted. Existing goals and typed totals are unchanged. A counted snapshot names its goal's entry ledger at that revision as its evidence, so a build without Q-17 reads it as a typed total.
rollback: Revert the Q-17 commit, or disable F-15's flag. Keep goal_observation and its entries. A build without Q-17 reads a counted snapshot as a typed total whose source is the entry ledger, so its reads keep working, but it accepts a typed total on such a goal.
limitations: Entries are the person's citations: user reported, never provider verified. No connected source records an entry automatically; that needs its own tested mapping, explicitly installed.
Things are matched by name without case, width or spacing differences; spelling variants (Acme Inc. and Acme) are not merged, the person corrects them.
Counts only. Amounts such as revenue stay on F-15's typed snapshot.
A counted measure holds at most 1,000 things; a goal keeps at most 20,000 entries, corrections included.
Parents and children are independent: no subtree union.
No dashboard presentation: D-track cards show entries and lineage.
found: F-15's typed total carries one citation for the whole number, so six signed partners could not be traced to six things, and a typed six and six evidenced partners looked the same.
Nothing recorded which partner a count included, so the same partner reported twice, or a partner who backed out, could not be told apart from real progress.
integration: Merge F-15 (#796) and its F stack first; main c06b16c1 has no goal measurements.

F-16 (#805) computes goal changes from goal_measurement_receipt rows only. A counted goal changes through goal_observation entries, so F-16 shows no change for it until it also reads entries (the count at the window's start and end by recordedAt), or Q-17 also writes a snapshot receipt per entry. Decide at integration; neither branch is wrong alone.

Shared files: src/brief/contracts.ts gains an optional measurementDefinition.basis; src/vault/goal-measurement-schema.ts gains goal_observation; the measurement routes file is refactored around one body reader.
next: Dashboard presentation of entries and lineage (D-track); a tested automatic mapping from a connected source, explicitly installed; amounts as cited entries. Separate cards.
